extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and other persons who practice or may practice before the USPTO (patent and trademark practitioners); OED/USPTO stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, definitions, procedural requirements, and sanctioning factors the USPTO uses to determine disciplinary jurisdiction and to evaluate misconduct by persons practicing (or offering to provide legal services) before the Office. Focused on unauthorized practice, specific ethics provisions, burden of proof, and sanction factors for suspension/exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary jurisdiction (37 C.F.R. § 11.19(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: All practitioners engaged in practice before the Office ... are subject to the disciplinary jurisdiction of the Office. A person not registered or recognized to practice before the USPTO is also subject to the Agency's disciplinary authority if the person provides or offers to provide any legal services before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the threshold for asserting USPTO discipline: filing trademark matters or providing legal services related to the Office can subject a person (including unregistered attorneys) to OED jurisdiction. The Final Order applies this provision to hold an unregistered attorney subject to discipline for providing patent legal services and for trademark practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'practice before the Office' (37 C.F.R. § 11.5(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Practice before the Office' includes any law-related service connected with presentation to the Office ... such presentations include preparing necessary documents in contemplation of filing the documents with the Office, corresponding and communicating with the Office, and representing a client through documents or at interviews, hearings, and meetings, as well as communicating with and advising a client concerning matters pending or contemplated to be presented before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as the operative definition to determine whether conduct constitutes practice: preparing documents, drafting filings, corresponding with examiners, advising clients about matters to be presented to the USPTO, and representing clients at proceedings are all encompassed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific activities constituting practice in patent matters (37 C.F.R. § 11.5(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice before the Office in patent matters includes, but is not limited to, preparing and prosecuting any patent application; consulting with or giving advice to a client in contemplation of filing a patent application or other document with the Office; drafting the specification or claims of a patent application; drafting an amendment or reply to a communication from the Office that may require written argument to establish the patentability of a claimed invention; drafting a reply to a communication from the Office regarding a patent application; and drafting a communication for a public use, interference, reexamination proceeding, petition, appeal to or any other proceeding before the Board, or other proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This non-exhaustive list is used to identify concrete acts (e.g., drafting claims, responding to office actions, advising on strategy) that amount to practice in patent matters; the Final Order lists multiple such acts as evidence of unauthorized practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice in trademark matters (37 C.F.R. § 11.5(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice before the Office in trademark matters includes, but is not limited to, consulting with or giving advice to a client in contemplation of filing a trademark application or other document with the Office; preparing and prosecuting an application for trademark registration; preparing an amendment which may require written argument to establish the registrability of the mark; and conducting an opposition, cancellation, or concurrent use proceeding; or conducting an appeal to the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even a single trademark filing or participation in TTAB proceedings subjects an attorney to USPTO disciplinary jurisdiction; the Final Order treats prior trademark practice as an independent basis for jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only registered practitioners may prosecute patent applications of others (37 C.F.R. § 11.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only practitioners who are registered under § 11.6 ... are permitted to prosecute patent applications of others before the Office or represent others in any proceedings before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-registration is not a defense to discipline for performing the prohibited activities; preparing and submitting patent filings for others is reserved to registered patent practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized practice of law (37 C.F.R. § 11.505)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not practice law in a jurisdiction in violation of the regulation of the legal profession in that jurisdiction, or assist another in doing so. The USPTO is considered a jurisdiction for the purposes of this rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to an unregistered attorney who provided patent legal services to clients (drafting responses, amended claims, advising strategy), holding such conduct to be the unauthorized practice of patent law before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representing a client when representation would violate rules or law (37 C.F.R. § 11.116(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits a practitioner from representing a client where the representation would result in a violation of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct or other law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to charge practitioners who engage in representation that conflicts with regulatory requirements (e.g., unregistered patent practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: False or misleading communications about practitioner's services (37 C.F.R. § 11.701)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes false or misleading communications regarding a practitioner's services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers misrepresentations to clients about the nature/scope of services or about whether the practitioner is authorized/registered to perform certain services; the Final Order cites false information provided to clients as a basis for violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice (former 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) and current § 11.804(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes engaging in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to address behavior that undermines the justice system generally; the Final Order finds unauthorized practice falls within this proscription.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (former § 10.23(b)(4) and § 11.804(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where communications or conduct to clients or the Office included deceptive representations; treated as a basis for discipline separate from unauthorized practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other misconduct that adversely reflects on fitness (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i) and § 11.804(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers other conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office, including committing a criminal act that reflects adversely on honesty, trustworthiness, or fitness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all provisions for conduct undermining a practitioner's fitness; cited among alleged violations in disciplinary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof: clear and convincing evidence (37 C.F.R. § 11.49)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must prove violations of the USPTO Code or USPTO Rules by clear and convincing evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard governing proof in USPTO disciplinary proceedings; the ALJ applied this standard in finding rule violations were established by the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for suspension or exclusion (37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b)(1)-(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: An ALJ initial decision that imposes exclusion or suspension must explain the reason after consideration of: (1) whether the practitioner violated a duty owed to a client, the public, the legal system, or the profession; (2) whether the practitioner acted intentionally, knowingly, or negligently; (3) the amount of actual or potential injury caused by the misconduct; and (4) the existence of any aggravating or mitigating factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ALJ must apply and explain these four factors when imposing suspension/exclusion; the Final Order analyzes each factor (duty violated, intent, injury, aggravating/mitigating) and uses them to justify an 18‑month suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggravating and mitigating factors (ABA Standards and examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggravating factors may include selfish motive, pattern of misconduct, multiple offenses, and substantial experience; mitigating factors may include absence of prior disciplinary record, good standing, and good intentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ALJ may reference ABA Standards when weighing sanction severity; the Final Order lists specific aggravating (paid fees for unauthorized work, repeated practice) and mitigating (no prior discipline, good standing, claimed good intentions) factors and balances them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions, remedial orders, and practitioner duties after discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Possible sanctions include suspension from practice before the USPTO (here 18 months); additional orders include publication of a Notice in the Official Gazette, notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts, dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and electronic accounts, prohibition on applying for or obtaining a Customer Number until reinstatement, and compliance with duties of a disciplined practitioner (37 C.F.R. § 11.58).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies concrete administrative consequences and post-discipline obligations; the Final Order prescribes publication language, dissociation, prohibitions regarding Customer Numbers, and notification duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice, publication, and state notification (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.59 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the stated form and give notice of the public discipline and reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where the practitioner is admitted and to courts where admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates public disclosure of discipline and inter-jurisdictional notification to state bars and courts; the Final Order orders specific publication and notice steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural rights: appeals, de novo review, reconsideration, and judicial review (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.55, 11.56 and 35 U.S.C. § 32)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may appeal an ALJ's Initial Decision to the USPTO Director within 30 days; the Director may conduct a de novo review and may affirm, reverse, modify, or remand; requests for reconsideration must be filed within 20 days; judicial review is available on the record in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia under 35 U.S.C. § 32 within 30 days after the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the procedural timeline and standards for post-ALJ review and further judicial remedies; the Final Order both follows and reminds parties of these deadlines and fora.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALJ explanation requirement for suspension/exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: An ALJ initial decision that imposes exclusion or suspension must explain the reason for imposing such a sanction after consideration of the four § 11.54(b) factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures that sanctions are reasoned and tied to enumerated factors; the Final Order assesses whether the ALJ sufficiently explained reasons and affirms where supported by the record.
